in the vicinity of Hama the decree of the Most High overtook him,
and his end arrived, and he died.
And his deep thoughts, which were full of arrogance, came to naught.
For this man had become so excessively arrogant in his soul
that he fell only a little short
of what the ancient Pharaoh said,
saying:
"The River Nile is mine,
and I made it."
It is said
that in that battle with the Tatars he was wounded by an arrow in his groin,
and the arrowhead remained in it for many days.
And when he ordered a surgeon to extract it,
as soon as he pulled it out,
his spirit departed.
And his son succeeded him in Egypt,
and he handed over the administration of all Syria to the lord of Hama.
Later, however, it was confirmed to us that his death was not thus,
but his treasurer mixed deadly poison in mare's milk and gave it to him to drink.
And when he felt the pain,
he commanded and they made the treasurer himself also drink from that milk,
and immediately both of them died together.
Now, something occurred in this battle that is worthy of record.
For they say
that when the Tatars were broken and their slain fell upon the ground,
Bunduqdar ordered the younger brother of Bar Katir,
the one who had fled to him,
to go around among the slain of the Tatars
and see which of the men of renown had been killed,
so that he might boast in this manner before the Egyptians.
And when that man went among the slain
and was turning their faces over to identify them,
there was among those slain a certain Tatar who was wounded and fallen down,
and was not yet dead,
but still had strength in him,
and was waiting for night to rise and flee.
And when he saw Bar Katir turning over the slain,
he thought that he was going around to kill those who were not completely dead.
And because, as he was,
with his armor bound on,
he was lying down,
he took his bow, drew an arrow from his quiver,
aimed skillfully straight at Bar Katir,
and struck him in his eye,
and the arrowhead plunged into his brain.
And those who were with him thought
that the arrow had flown at him from heaven;
and they carried him and brought him before Bunduqdar,
and in that very hour he died.
